clue.text: Outward appearance of a cad eccentric? Not entirely (6)

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the words before it, not all of them

blocks.note: oF A CAD Eccentric, running across four words

annotation.surface: Someone suspects a cad's eccentricity is only a front.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not entirely' read as doubt about the cad, but they tell you the answer is only partly there in the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from architecture: the front face of a building, extended to any show put on for the world.

clue.text: More distant male relation, right to be included (7)

indicators.note: to be included is to be taken inside something, so R goes within the relation

blocks.note: a parent who is a man

annotation.surface: A more distant male relative insists he has a right to be in the family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More distant male relation' reads as one phrase, like a second cousin; the definition stops after 'More distant'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the comparative of far, used of physical distance.

clue.text: Priest’s collection of holy books (5)

blocks.note: a cleric attached to a cathedral
the accepted list of books making up a scripture

annotation.surface: A priest owns a shelf of holy books.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive is a trick: read '’s' as 'is', and the priest and the collection are two meanings of one word.
annotation.definitionFit: One word covers both a cathedral clergyman and the authorised body of sacred texts, as in the biblical canon.

clue.text: Some foreign currency in fall? (7)

indicators.note: tells you to translate 'Some' into another language, here French

blocks.note: a coin, a hundredth of a dollar or euro

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bit of foreign money is losing value.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some foreign currency' reads as one phrase about money, but 'foreign' belongs to 'Some': it asks for a translation, not an exotic coin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drop or downward movement, as in the plane's descent.

clue.text: Did Caesar, being a calculating type, count on one? (6)

definitions.text: Did Caesar, being a calculating type, count on one?

blocks.note: the surface wants a scheming politician; the setter means a Roman doing sums
the surface hears relying on an ally; the setter means doing arithmetic on a device

annotation.surface: Was scheming Julius Caesar someone who relied on a trusted ally?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calculating' suggests a schemer and 'count on' suggests trust; read literally, a Roman doing arithmetic counted on beads in a frame.
annotation.definitionFit: The bead frame was the Roman calculator, so it is literally what Caesar would count on.

clue.text: Be ill in bed – get released on condition (6)

indicators.note: in the surface a patient lies in bed; the same word puts the letters for 'be ill' inside BED

blocks.note: to ail is to be unwell

annotation.surface: A patient laid up in bed is waiting to be let go on terms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In bed' reads as where the patient is lying; it is the whole instruction. The dash marks where the wordplay ends and the definition starts.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: someone let out of custody on a promise to return has been granted bail.

clue.text: Plant cleaned, repositioned outside home (9)

indicators.note: the letters of CLEANED are moved to new places
the rearranged letters stand outside IN, wrapping it

blocks.note: in = at home, as in 'staying in'

annotation.surface: A factory was cleaned and moved to a site beyond the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory being cleaned up and relocated; it is a wild flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the lesser celandine is a small yellow wild flower of British hedgerows.

clue.text: Temporarily stop American writer entering borders of Scotland (7)

indicators.note: US and PEN go into the letters around them
take just the edges of Scotland, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: An American author is halted at the Scottish frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but here it is the instrument, not the person.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to halt something for a while, as a match is suspended for rain.

clue.text: Led by devil, I start out on protest march maybe (13)

indicators.note: what follows is led by the devil, so DEMON goes at the front
the letters of I START are put out of order

annotation.surface: Egged on by some devil, a protester sets off on a march.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start out' reads as setting off; 'out' alone is the instruction on I START. 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a protest march is one kind of public show of feeling.

clue.text: Member of family showing rancour to some extent (4)

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: A relative is showing a bit of bitterness.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between 'showing' and 'rancour', so look across word boundaries.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the familiar short form for a grandmother, one relation among many.

clue.text: Iciest Alps to be dealt with? Expert needed (10)

indicators.note: like cards being dealt, the letters are shuffled out anew

annotation.surface: Tackling the iciest Alpine slopes calls for a professional.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is mountaineering: frozen peaks need an expert guide, so 'to be dealt with' sounds like tackling the climb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone with deep knowledge of one narrow field.

clue.text: Alter money handed back to customer? (6)

blocks.note: a noun: the coins returned at the till after overpaying

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether to fiddle the money given back at the till.
annotation.walkthrough: One word does both jobs, a verb and a noun; the question mark flags the second, looser definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means to make different, and the noun is the balance returned when you pay too much.

clue.text: Shrub, one confused with alder (8)

indicators.note: the letters of ONE and ALDER are mixed up together

annotation.surface: A shrub that people mistake for an alder tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a botanical mix-up; 'with' just puts ONE and ALDER together as one heap of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a poisonous evergreen with pink or white flowers, common in Mediterranean gardens.

clue.text: Most intelligent, supreme? That’s about right (9)

indicators.note: the word for supreme is about, meaning around, what follows

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether the smartest is also the finest, and is told that's roughly true.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's about right' sounds like agreement; 'about' is the instruction to wrap.
annotation.definitionFit: Bright is the everyday word for clever, and this is its superlative.

clue.text: Digger Ann working, doing this? (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new order

annotation.surface: Ann is out digging, and we are asked what she is up to.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters of Ann the digger rearrange into what she is busy doing.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue asks what a woman out digging is up to, and tending the beds is the likeliest answer.

clue.text: Good-natured type (4)

blocks.note: a noun: a sort or variety

annotation.walkthrough: 'Good-natured type' reads as a pleasant person; it is two meanings, an adjective and a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means warm-hearted, and the noun means a sort, as in 'of that kind'.

clue.text: Island’s second rescue vessel (4)

blocks.note: s = second, as in units of time
Noah's boat that saved the animals from the flood

annotation.surface: An island keeps a backup lifeboat.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' here means 'has', not possession. 'Second' looks like a spare lifeboat; it is the unit of time.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy, famous for banning cars.

clue.text: Bear’s belly (7)

blocks.note: a verb: to put up with
a noun: the paunch or tummy

annotation.surface: A bear's big belly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb 'to tolerate'. The '’s' just stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means to tolerate, as in 'I can't stomach him', and the noun is the tummy.

clue.text: Time to meet odd disciple, a musician (9)

blocks.note: one of the twelve apostles, the fisherman

annotation.surface: It's time to meet a strange follower who plays music.
annotation.walkthrough: RUM here is the British adjective for strange, as in 'a rum business', not the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a player of the brass instrument is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Generator a gent repaired in next to no time (7)

indicators.note: the letters of A GENT are put back together differently
the rearranged letters go inside the word for next to no time

blocks.note: a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

annotation.surface: A man fixes a generator in a flash.
annotation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment, so 'in next to no time' is both the speed of the repair and the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a small electrical generator using permanent magnets, as in old engine ignitions.

clue.text: A gentle drunk being refined (7)

indicators.note: the letters stagger about into a new order

annotation.surface: A mild-mannered drunk still manages to be classy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' sits after 'gentle', looking like a noun for a tippler; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: graceful and stylish in manner or appearance.

clue.text: Item of clothing that is hidden under spade? (6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, IE comes below CARD

blocks.note: a spade is a playing card, not only a garden tool
with 'is' it makes 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

annotation.surface: Something to wear has been stashed beneath a garden spade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That is' does double duty: it is i.e., and the 'is' also carries the surface sentence along.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: short for cardigan, a knitted jacket that buttons down the front.

clue.text: Witches and social worker establishing agreement (8)

blocks.note: a social insect of the worker caste

annotation.surface: A group of witches and a social worker draw up a pact.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is a job title in the surface; here it is an insect that lives in colonies.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: a binding promise, as in a biblical or legal pact.

clue.text: Georgia dying initially to obtain useful device (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'dying'

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for the US state

annotation.surface: Georgia, near death, is desperate to lay hands on a handy tool.
annotation.walkthrough: Georgia looks like a woman's name; it is the state, abbreviated GA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small ingenious tool or appliance.

clue.text: Gloomy music awful – little good in it (5)

indicators.note: 'it' points back to the word for awful, and G goes in it

blocks.note: G, a little abbreviation for good

annotation.surface: A critic says a mournful piece is terrible, with barely anything to recommend it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little good' reads as faint praise; 'little' asks for the abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a slow lament, originally sung at funerals.

clue.text: Unchanged after setback, madam is one such (10)

definitions.text: Unchanged after setback, madam is one such

blocks.note: the surface hears someone unshaken by misfortune; the setter means a word written backwards that stays the same
the surface makes a lady the subject; the setter offers MADAM as a specimen word

annotation.surface: A lady stays unshaken after a disappointment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setback' suggests a misfortune; read it as 'set back', written backwards. MADAM survives that unchanged.
annotation.definitionFit: The term for a word reading the same both ways, and MADAM is the textbook example.

clue.text: Perch across a highway (4)

indicators.note: the perch stretches across A, lying either side of it

blocks.note: an old British measure of length, 5.5 yards, also called a pole

annotation.surface: A bird sits on a branch hanging over a main road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a bird's seat or a fish; it is the old unit of length.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any public way for traffic, though highway sounds grander.

clue.text: Superior charter, we hear (6)

indicators.note: the answer is what the word for charter sounds like

blocks.note: to charter a boat or plane is to rent it

annotation.surface: A grander founding document is being talked about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charter' looks like a noun, a founding document; it is the verb. In British speech, which drops the final R, the two words sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: above in rank or quality, as in a higher court.

clue.text: Decent little house, comfy home (6)

blocks.note: a cosy home, as a bird makes

annotation.surface: A modest little house that makes a cosy home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little' tells you to shorten house to its abbreviation, as seen in addresses.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: upright and truthful, as in 'an honest day's work'.
